title: Back to Europe, leaving Willy Lewis for Ricco's Creole Band in Norway
summary: When war broke out he left after being insulted by Burns at rehearsal, joined a Cuban band, Ricco's Creole Band, and toured Norway, where he started a small jazz club.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So, all right, after I had taken care of all of my business I went back. But now, this is in the summertime, I went back. And when I got back, the war was in -- so, I said, well, I'll go to Sweden, I can make my way around Europe now.
So now, all right, I was supposed to go back with Willie Lewis and we was supposed to go to Knokke.
All right, but it seems that at rehearsal that Burns insulted me or something and I got up and left. I got up and left and got a job with a Cuban band, Ricco's Creole Band.

Creole band. He played the flute so we went up to Norway and then we would play that stuff now the Norwegans were not aware of jazz, they were aware of it faintly and every night I got off, there was a few fellows up there, they could, they was trying to play so they created a little jazz club and I played and it seems that later they would come in and say I would like to play a few jazz numbers slow.
So, I did this and I became very liked in
Norway and everybody was happy too. We had one boy played the trombone named John degrass. (phonetic)
